name: talaria-daily-driver-verdict-restatement
description: Close DRIFT-04, the last open finding of the R1-R40 conformance audit: the v0.1 daily-driver verdict grades R2 and R3 unmet on reasons that stopped being true on 2026-08-04. Re-grade those rows against the live corpus, re-read the rows the finding never mentions, restate the verdict on the corrected table, and close the finding out.

units.label: Re-grade the R2 and R3 rows against the live corpus, with citations
units.worth_it_because: These two rows were graded carelessly once already and that is the entire defect; a re-grade that flips them to met on weak citations makes the release gate say something false in the opposite direction, which is the one outcome the plan exists to prevent.
units.prompt: U1: Re-grade the daily-driver verdict's R2 and R3 rows (evidence-table rows 17 and 18) against the live recordings, updating them in place with citations to the specific frames that settle each. Read docs/plans/2026-08-05-daily-driver-verdict-restatement-plan.md (unit U1) as your authoritative spec.

units.label: Re-read rows 6, 13 and 19 and the five what-would-change items, reporting what has NOT moved
units.worth_it_because: This is the unit that resists confirmation pressure. Four rows were graded against a client that had never attached and it has now attached, so every row reads as improved; establishing that row 6 has not moved, against that pull, is judgment work and is the plan's falsifiability control.
units.prompt: U2: Re-read evidence-table rows 6, 13 and 19 and the five 'What would change this verdict' items against current evidence, and state the present position of each -- including, explicitly, the ones that have not moved. Do not restate the verdict. Read docs/plans/2026-08-05-daily-driver-verdict-restatement-plan.md (unit U2) as your authoritative spec.

units.label: Restate the verdict on the corrected table, and correct the four stale sentences that cite it
units.worth_it_because: The verdict is the artifact that gates the v0.1 release. Applying the document's own any-gap-blocks rule to a table two other units just rewrote, without presupposing the outcome, is the highest-stakes judgment in the plan.
units.prompt: U3: Restate the verdict on the table U1 and U2 produced, applying the document's own rule that any gap blocks a ready verdict, and correct the four now-false sentences that cite it -- README.md's 'Read the verdict before you rely on it' paragraph, run_live's docstring in talaria/cli.py, both stale sentences in talaria/ui/app.py (the twelve-versus-thirteen count and open_session's docstring), and the R2-is-unmet clause in tests/transport/test_session_startup.py. Each records what it used to say. Read docs/plans/2026-08-05-daily-driver-verdict-restatement-plan.md (unit U3) as your authoritative spec.

units.label: Close DRIFT-04 out across the register, the worklist and the index
units.prompt: U4: Close DRIFT-04 out -- move its register entry to Resolved findings with the closing commit, update the register's counts and status header, remove its P1 entry from QUEUED.md, fix the docs/analysis/README.md cross-reference, correct the register's own wrong 'exactly two things' claim in place, file the LEARNINGS.md and DECISIONS.md entries, and file the deferred QUEUED.md entry for the general stale-gating-document problem. Dated plan artifacts are historical record and are left unedited. Read docs/plans/2026-08-05-daily-driver-verdict-restatement-plan.md (unit U4) as your authoritative spec.
